title: SLO rollout readiness and capacity checklist
author: Priya Raman
body:
Overview

This checklist is a prescriptive, step-by-step readiness guide for rolling out new or tightened SLOs for production services. It combines SLO definition sanity checks, capacity validation tests, canary deployment procedures, alert and dashboard configuration, and rollback/mitigation criteria. Use this document when proposing any change that will affect customer-facing latency or availability SLOs.

Goals
- Ensure SLOs are realistic and measurable before deployment.
- Validate capacity and autoscaling behavior under expected and burst traffic.
- Confirm observability, alerts, and playbooks are in place for rapid mitigation.
- Reduce blast radius with progressive rollouts and automatic fallbacks.

Scope and ownership
- Applies to: customer-facing inference endpoints (api/redwood-gen, api/redwood-chat), embeddings services (embed-service), internal admin APIs.
- Primary owner: SRE oncall for the service (team: serving-runtime).
- Stakeholders: product manager, service reliability engineer, backend owner, infra capacity owner.

High-level readiness checklist (must be completed and signed off)
1) SLO & metric review (owner: service PM + SRE)
   - Confirm SLO type (latency / availability / correctness) and measurement window.
   - Example SLOs to validate:
     * Latency: p95 request latency <= 250ms, p99 <= 700ms (for small-gen route, 1–512 tokens).
     * Availability: successful_response_rate >= 99.95% (30d rolling).
     * Embeddings throughput: tail latency p99 <= 120ms under steady-state 50 QPS.
   - Ensure the SLO definition references the correct metric source: telemetry.ingest -> metrics.redwood.{service}.{metric}.
   - Confirm labels and tags are consistent for multi-region aggregation (region, pod_group, model_variant).

2) Error budget & escalation policy (owner: SRE lead)
   - Compute projected error budget burn for first 7/30 days with expected load.
   - Define triggers:
     * Burn rate > 5x for 1h -> paging to oncall.
     * Cumulative 3% burn in 24h -> incident review required.
   - Confirm runbook references: local rollback, traffic routing to fallback model_variant, and capacity surge procedures.

3) Capacity & autoscaling validation (owner: infra/capacity)
   - Prepare capacity test harness: k6 or vegeta script in infra/tests/capacity with service-specific profiles.
   - Run two-phase load tests against a staging cluster that mirrors production config:
     1. Sustained test: 1.5x expected peak for 30 minutes.
     2. Spike test: 3x expected peak for 3 minutes, then return to 1x, repeat 3 times.
   - Pass criteria (all must be met):
     * p95 and p99 latency remain below SLO thresholds for sustained test.
     * No more than 0.2% elevated error rate during sustained test.
     * Autoscaler scales pods/instances within configured scale-up window: <= 120s for horizontal scaling events.
     * No OOM or CPU throttling events in node metrics.
   - Required artifacts: load test logs, JMeter/k6 script, node GPU/CPU utilization graphs.

4) Fallback and graceful degradation strategy (owner: runtime)
   - Define fallback routing policies in router-config:fallback_policies -> prefer-region, then fallback_model_variant (quantized or smaller model).
   - Confirm cache warming and prefix-KV behavior when routing changes occur.
   - Validate degraded mode behavior: reduced tokens-per-request limit and shorter sequence length cap.

5) Observability and alerting (owner: observability)
   - Dashboards: create a per-service rollout dashboard with: SLO windowed burn, latency (p50/p95/p99), error_rate, QPS, concurrency, queue_length, provisioned_instances.
   - Alerts (examples):
     * slo_burn_rate_1h > 3 -> P1 page to oncall (pagerduty).
     * p99_latency > SLO_threshold + 150ms for 5m -> P2 alert.
     * cpu_throttle_rate > 0.05 -> warn (slack).
   - Ensure tracing is enabled for 100% sampled requests during canary windows to assist in triage.

6) Runbook & playbook attachments (owner: SRE)
   - Attach or link the following pre-written playbooks:
     * rapid-mitigation-for-availability.json (traffic cutover + fallback)
     * scale-up-resources.sh (IaC script to add reserved capacity)
     * rollback-deployment.md (how to revert canary / force stable).
   - Include a 5-step quick action list at top of runbook for oncall:
     1. Identify scope (region/model_variant).
     2. Route traffic to fallback.
     3. Add capacity if autoscaler hasn’t responded.
     4. Revert code change if introduced in last deploy.
     5. Declare incident and start postmortem if error budget burn is sustained.

7) Canary rollout plan (owner: release engineer)
   - Canary phases (example):
     * Phase A (5% traffic) for 30m with 100% tracing and stricter alerts.
     * Phase B (25% traffic) for 60m.
     * Phase C (50% traffic) for 2h.
     * Phase D (100% traffic).
   - Success gating criteria between phases:
     * No P1 pages.
     * 1h slo_burn_rate <= 2x baseline.
     * Latency delta (canary vs baseline p95) < 20%.
   - Automated rollback: if any phase fails gating criteria, traffic must be routed back to previous stable variant within 10 minutes.

8) Compliance and data-safety check (owner: security/compliance)
   - Verify no new PII fields are added to logs/metrics.
   - Confirm KMS usage for any new secrets and that audit logging is enabled.

9) Communication and run-deck (owner: release manager)
   - Pre-rollout: email + slack channel with schedule, expected blast radius, and rollback window.
   - During rollout: provide minute-by-minute status in channel; oncall posts updates every 15 minutes during canary phases.
   - Post-rollout: 72-hour observation period where daily SLO burn updates are required.

10) Post-deploy verification and retrospective (owner: SRE lead)
   - 24h verification: run synthetic user journeys (end-to-end) and confirm p99 latency is within target across regions.
   - 72h verification: monitor error budget consumption and confirm trend.
   - Run a short incident review if any rollback or >5% error budget burn occurred.

Example validation table (to paste into a release checklist)
| Item | Owner | Target/Threshold | Evidence required | Status |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| p99 latency (primary region) | SRE | <= 700ms | dashboard link / screenshot | TODO |
| Autoscaler response time | Infra | <= 120s | scale event logs | TODO |
| Error rate | Service owner | <= 0.05% | metrics export | TODO |
| Canary rollback window | Release engineer | <= 10 min | routing logs | TODO |

Commands and snippets
- Run a canary traffic split (kubectl / router API example):

kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: routing.redwood/v1
kind: TrafficSplit
metadata:
  name: myservice-canary
spec:
  backends:
  - name: myservice-stable
    weight: 95
  - name: myservice-canary
    weight: 5
EOF

- Quick load test (k6 example):

k6 run --vus 200 --duration 30m tests/k6/slo-profile-smallgen.js

- Query SLO burn from metrics API (example):

curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $METRIC_TOKEN" "https://metrics.redwood/api/v1/slo/burn?service=myservice&window=1h" | jq .

Sign-off checklist (required approvers before moving from canary->full):
- [ ] Service PM (product correctness)
- [ ] SRE lead (observability & runbooks)
- [ ] Infra capacity owner (scaling artifacts)
- [ ] Release engineer (rollback automation)
- [ ] Security reviewer (data handling)

Appendix: common failure modes and mitigations
- Slow tail latency under burst: investigate queue_length, model_variant cold-starts, and excessive batching. Temporary mitigation: reduce max_batch_window and route to smaller model_variant.
- Autoscaler lag: increase scale target steps and add emergency reserve pool.
- Increased error rate from a new model: immediate rollback to previous model_variant and open a P1 to triage training / tokenization edge cases.
